title: one owed decision, as its consumers read it (the fold of owed-decisions.jsonl)
description: The current state of one decision, which is a different shape from the rows it is folded from and therefore a different schema. `owed-decisions.jsonl` is an append-only log of EVENTS -- 'raised' is a thing that happened, and a decision is not raised twice -- so the log cannot carry a state token without describing states it can never hold. This is what every consumer of the record actually wants: the question, its severity, and the state it is in right now, with `state` and `severity` required because a reader that has to infer either one is a reader writing its own copy of a rule this file exists to state once.

state.description: Where the decision stands. 'open' is waiting on a person; the log's corresponding event is 'raised', and translating between them is this projection's job rather than every consumer's.

severity.description: Whether an unanswered decision refuses the close. Derived from the class when the decision is raised and never settable per call: a severity a caller could set is a severity a caller could lower, and the class that blocks is the one no caller may opt out of.

options.description: Two or more, always: a question with one answer is a notification.

event.description: The last event folded into this record. Carried so a reader can trace the state back to the row that produced it; `state` is what a reader should branch on.
